title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Criminals have used deepfake technology to impersonate specific individuals, including a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to defraud immigrants. The impersonations occurred on social media and through phone calls, where synthesized voices and spoofed numbers made the fraud appear credible. The scams targeted vulnerable populations seeking legal services and investment opportunities, with reported losses in the hundreds of thousands of dollars.

The failure happened at the point where potential victims could not verify the identity of the person contacting them. Audio deepfakes were made using samples from social media, and phone number spoofing allowed scammers to appear as trusted contacts. To have caught these impersonations, victims would have needed to verify requests through independently confirmed phone numbers or established secret code words rather than trusting audio and caller identification alone.

It is not established whether the generative AI tools themselves were deployed without appropriate safeguards, or whether the tools were used outside their intended conditions. The summary describes how criminals misused available technology rather than how AI systems operated by companies or institutions failed in deployment.

summary:
Criminals are increasingly using artificial intelligence to commit scams across Georgia and South Florida by creating deepfakes of voices, photos, and phone calls to impersonate trusted individuals. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice and identity were cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans reported nearly $893 million in AI-enabled scam losses last year, with Florida reporting 350 AI-related complaints totaling $39.9 million and Georgia reporting 71 complaints totaling $10.4 million.

Law enforcement officials warn that generative AI is making traditional scams like romance schemes, fake investment opportunities, and grandparent scams much more convincing. Scammers use audio samples from social media to clone voices, research family relationships, and spoof legitimate phone numbers. Experts recommend establishing secret code words with family members, verifying urgent requests through known phone numbers, and avoiding immediate action on unexpected money requests. As AI tools become cheaper and more accessible, investigators predict these scams will continue evolving, making verification procedures critical to protecting consumers.
